subject.title: Feature request: Escalating stall recovery for sub-agents (nudge → kill)

question: Should OpenClaw add a two-stage subagent inactivity recovery contract now, and which owner should define the activity source, thresholds, nudge/kill semantics, default behavior, and user-visible terminal notifications?
rationale: The remaining work changes recovery policy, defaults/config, session state, and message delivery semantics, and current main already has overlapping diagnostic recovery and explicit timeout enforcement that need consolidation rather than blind additive implementation.

options.title: Define one core recovery contract
options.body: Use existing diagnostics, subagent control, and session activity surfaces where possible, then specify tests and proof for nudge, kill, parent wake, and channel-visible terminal behavior.

options.title: Prototype default-off watchdog
options.body: Add an experimental opt-in watchdog with narrow config and clear non-default behavior while leaving current diagnostics and runTimeoutSeconds defaults intact.

options.title: Defer to adjacent mechanisms
options.body: Close or narrow this request in favor of existing diagnostic abort recovery, explicit runTimeoutSeconds, manual kill/reap in #87445, and session activity/watchdog work in #39127/#39141.

recommendation.title: Define one core recovery contract
recommendation.body: Use existing diagnostics, subagent control, and session activity surfaces where possible, then specify tests and proof for nudge, kill, parent wake, and channel-visible terminal behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a product policy and user-visible recovery decision, and issue routing already points this handle at the subagent/Telegram reliability decision space.
